source.ref: Features p.1 ('SOT-666 and SOT23-6L packages'); §3.2 SOT-666 package information p.14

value.note: Both packages are 6-pin. The device is a monolithic array: two data-line channels plus a VBUS rail clamp, which is why it needs six pins rather than the two of a single-line diode.

source.ref: Features p.1 (SOT-666 / SOT23-6L, both 6-lead); package outlines §3, p.14+

value.note: ST does not publish a row literally named VRWM. 5.25 V is the reverse voltage at which leakage is specified (IRM at VRM = 5.25 V, typ 10 nA / max 150 nA), and the datasheet revision history records that this figure was set 'as specified in USB standard' — i.e. it is the intended standing rail voltage, 5 V VBUS plus tolerance. The breakdown voltage VBR between VBUS and GND is separately given as min 6 V at IR = 1 mA, so the device does not begin conducting until above the USB rail.

value.note: Clamping voltage rises with surge current, so a single number would understate it under a real strike. Both figures are for any I/O pin to GND with an 8/20 us pulse. The datasheet also gives the analytical form in §2.1: VCL+ = VTRANSIL + VF, with VTRANSIL = VBR + Rd_TRANSIL x IP, and works an example at IEC 61000-4-2 level 4 contact discharge (8 kV through 330 ohm, so about 24 A) using typical Rd = 0.5 ohm.

value.note: MAXIMUM I/O-to-GND capacitance at VR = 1.65 V (typical 2.5 pF). This is the number that makes the part usable on USB 2.0 high-speed lines at 480 Mb/s, and it is roughly 20x lower than a general-purpose ESD diode such as the PESD5V0L1BA at 75 pF. Two related figures matter for differential integrity: I/O-to-I/O capacitance is typ 1.2 / max 1.7 pF, and the I/O-to-GND matching tolerance is 0.015 pF, which the datasheet calls out as giving consistent D+/D- balance compliant with USB 2.0 requirements.

source.ref: Table 2 Electrical characteristics, Ci/o-GND, dCi/o-GND, Ci/o-i/o rows, p.2; Features and Benefits, p.1

value.note: Two data-line channels (D+ and D-), plus a separate clamp on VBUS which the datasheet lists as its own feature ('Protects VBUS') rather than as a third data channel. So one USBLC6-2 covers a complete USB 2.0 port. ESD rating is IEC 61000-4-2 level 4: 15 kV air discharge and 8 kV contact discharge, guaranteed at device level.
